phase_name: Fixture-Corpus Shellcheck Acceptance and Complete Hint Coverage

objectives.description: Replace the real-corpus pair in test-lint-shellcheck-parallel.sh's acceptance case with a fixture-corpus assertion: one process per file, worker cap honoured, discovery-order output, plus finding-set equivalence on the fixture. Keep the existing determinism and seeded-violation cases unchanged.

Replace the relative wall-clock ratio gate on the default path with a dispatch-shape assertion that does not require two corpus walks (observed peak concurrent shellcheck processes / per-file dispatch count)
Keep the real-corpus timing experiment available but opt-in behind an explicit env var the default path skips, with a header note that it is run deliberately; do not delete it

Hint every suite this work added or left unhinted (test-lint-shellcheck-parallel.sh, test-gate-registry-resolution.sh, test-check-record-versioning.sh; test-gate-cache-lib.sh and test-measure-gate-costs.sh already hinted by Phase 5)
Add an advisory hint-coverage check to run-all.sh so a newly added suite cannot land unhinted silently (never refuses a run, per suite-cost-hints.txt's own advisory-only header)

approaches_tried.approach: External process monitoring of real `shellcheck` concurrency via a `kill -0 PID` loop sampling `pgrep -f` counts, to observe dispatch-shape (worker cap honoured, peak concurrency) without walking the real corpus
approaches_tried.reason: guard-destructive-git.sh's sibling bounded-waiter hook (validate-bounded-waiter.sh) blocks any Bash-tool command shaped as a `kill -0` liveness loop combined with a `pgrep -f`/`ps | grep` process-name match, per bounded-build-waiter.md's self-match prohibition -- even though this usage was a sampling instrument, not a liveness test. Abandoned in favor of a PATH-substituted stub `shellcheck` binary that self-logs start/end timestamps and argv, letting peak concurrency be computed deterministically from the log after the run completes, with no live process polling at all.

approaches_tried.approach: PATH-substituted stub `shellcheck` binary (logs PID, start/end wall-clock ms, and full argv to a file; sleeps a fixed 0.4s window; exits 0) driving lint-shellcheck.sh over a 9-file fixture with a forced SHELLCHECK_JOBS=3 cap
approaches_tried.reason: Prototyped and verified directly: 9 invocations observed (one per fixture file), every invocation named exactly one fixture-dir file (no batched multi-file dispatch), and peak concurrency computed via an interval-overlap sweep over the sorted START/END timestamps equalled exactly 3 (the forced cap) across repeated runs. Deterministic and fast (<2s total vs. the prior ~120s real-corpus pair) because the stub's fixed sleep window gives a wide timing margin regardless of fork/exec overhead or host load.
